tweets.text:
Agent work in Computer is long-running, stateful, and branching, and has to survive restarts.

A SPACE sandbox outlives the request that created it and the connection carrying its output. It can pause, fork, or suspend to a memory and disk snapshot, then wake where it left off.

Agents in Computer run commands, install packages, and call external services with root access inside the sandbox.

The host stays outside the guest's control, and a per-sandbox gateway enforces egress policy on every outbound connection.

tweets.text:
This is one of the most important results in AI, period.

TLDR: neural networks are not tangled knots (polysemanticity is wrong). You can study their own neurons directly, without first "unfolding" them with a second model. 90% of neurons in Qwen-32B have one job.

Nick Cammarata started OpenAI’s interpretability team and is at Goodfire now. He’s been studying how LLMs work for a decade.

The stakes for understanding and aligning model behavior are the highest it’s ever been. Models have achieved superhuman results in math, can break production software systems, and changes the nature of white collar work. This work may finally allow us to intentionally design LLMs and shape how they behave.

Its a long, phenomenal read.
